description: Explains weather in plain terms for conversation: why it feels colder than the temperature, whether rain will matter on a hike, whether wind matters, whether the trail will be muddy, humidity, fog, frost, pressure. It separates what the forecast says (facts, each labelled forecast or formula) from what we are reasoning (inferences, each with its basis and how sure we are) and lists what we cannot see (unknowns). Pass the question as asked, or a topic. If it cannot tell what was asked it says so and gives the general picture.

activity.description: What the person is doing, if known. One of: walking, hiking, trail_running, road_running, cycling, camping, hunting, fishing, yard_work, construction, painting_finishing, general_outdoor. Plain words work too ("run", "hike", "stain the deck"). "Running" with no more words is treated as road_running.

duration_hours.description: How many hours to look at. Default 6.

latitude.description: Latitude in degrees. Use with longitude instead of location.

location.description: A place name such as "Glenbeulah, WI" or "Greenbush, Wisconsin", or coordinates as "43.79,-88.05". Add the state or country for small towns, because a bare "Greenbush" matches several places.

longitude.description: Longitude in degrees, west negative. Use with latitude instead of location.

question.description: The question as the person asked it, for example "Why does it feel colder than the temperature?".

start_time.description: The time the question is about. Defaults to now. An ISO 8601 time such as 2026-10-03T18:00:00-05:00 (read in the place's own time zone when it has no offset), or plain words: "now", "tonight", "tomorrow morning", "Saturday", "6 PM", "between 6 PM and midnight". A bare hour with no AM or PM is refused rather than guessed.

topic.description: The topic, if you know it. Otherwise it is read from the question.

units.description: imperial (F, mph, inches) or metric (C, km/h, mm). Defaults to imperial in the United States and metric elsewhere.

name: explain_weather
title: Explain the weather
